command_or_fixture: Read the spec; whitespace count of the report ADOPT 1 sentence (23 words, one action) which the rule passes but the plan rejects
counterexample_or_failure_condition: A one-action sentence of 21 or 26 words fails AC-3 or AC-5, although the guide says length is a prompt and not a limit.
expected: Acceptance uses the rule's own test: one action or one point per sentence
known_bad_detection_method: Counted the report ADOPT 1 sentence at 23 words with one action and showed AC-3 as written rejects what the rule accepts.
limitations: Plan review only; the guide is not yet edited
observed: Acceptance uses a numeric cap counted by the reviewer
proposition: Requirement 7, AC-3 and AC-5 enforce at most 20 and 25 words by reviewer count, which is a hard sentence limit.

disposition_rationale: Repair is to replace the cap with the one-action-or-one-point test in Requirement 7, AC-3 and AC-5; no linter.

command_or_fixture: Read Requirement 2 and applied both readings to AC-4, AC-6 and tasks 5 and 8; read report ADOPT 2 (report line 199) and passages 9 and 10
counterexample_or_failure_condition: No unit of verification is named. Under a strict reading (one command or one observation verifies every part), AC-4 holds three results from two commands and AC-6 holds four results verified at two different times (the close summary at close). Under a lax reading, one test run exempts passages 9 and 10.
expected: An exception that a writer can apply, such as 'unless one command or one observation verifies every part', and spec items that meet it or state why they pass
known_bad_detection_method: Strict reading applied to the spec's own AC-4 and AC-6 fails both, so the strict check catches a known multi-result item.
limitations: Plan review only. The guide is not yet edited. The decision between strict and lax wording belongs to the planner and operator.
observed: The exception has no unit. The spec's AC-4 and AC-6 fail the strict reading, and the lax reading exempts the cases the rule targets.
proposition: The Requirement 2 sentence 'unless its parts are always verified together' is decidable, and the spec's own items follow the rule.
public_path: docs/waves/241c3 writing-guide-sentence-structure/240wz-doc writing-guide-sentence-structure.md Requirement 2, AC-4, AC-6, Tasks
safety_and_authorization: Read-only; no repository edits

disposition_rationale: A bounded wording repair before readiness. It adds no linter, gate or limit.

command_or_fixture: Read the candidate guide's length paragraph and each added sentence; compared with report ADOPT 1 wording 'If it carries more, split it, and move three or more parallel cases into a list.'
counterexample_or_failure_condition: Read as written, Requirement 3.5 is unconditional. Sentence 1.5 lists 'handoffs, status records and review evidence', 1.6 lists 'the subject, the verb and the articles', and Requirement 2 lists 'A task, checklist item or acceptance criterion', each inline. The recommended CHANGELOG bullet puts four cases inline. AC-3 does not check this rule.
expected: The list rule is scoped to a sentence that carries more than one point, and every added sentence meets it
known_bad_detection_method: The literal list rule applied to the added sentences flags three inline three-item series.
limitations: Plan review only. A reader may infer the scope from the preceding sentence, but the guide's agent readers act on each sentence as written.
observed: The rule is a standalone sentence with no referent to the long sentence, and three added sentences plus the CHANGELOG bullet break its literal reading
proposition: Each added sentence follows the rules it adds (Requirement 7), including 'Move three or more parallel cases into a list.'

command_or_fixture: Computed sqrt(2p(1-p)/n) times 1.96 from report tables at .wavefoundry/work/241c3/eval/ste-review-report.md lines 59 to 103
counterexample_or_failure_condition: Product Intent says to compare four figures and that 'a difference of a few points is not evidence', but names no threshold, no reader and no action. Two-sample 95% half-widths from the report's sample sizes: task items about 12 points (n=118, p=36.4%), changelog over-25 about 7 points (n=285; no-rule drift was 5 points), spec over-25 about 2.3 points (n=2,062). Noun stacks halved with no rule and over-count by about half, so they cannot attribute an effect.
expected: A stated movement that counts as an effect (for example, task items below about 24%), who reads the re-run and what they do, or a plain statement that the re-run is descriptive
known_bad_detection_method: The report's own no-rule changelog drift of 5 points falls inside the 7-point interval, showing an unthresholded comparison cannot separate noise from effect.
limitations: Intervals assume independent sentences, which overstates precision. The handoff denominator is not reported, so its interval is an estimate.
observed: No decision rule, no threshold, no owner; only 'a difference of a few points is not evidence'
proposition: Product Intent names a post-release measure that can tell an effect from noise, or says honestly that it cannot.
public_path: docs/waves/241c3 writing-guide-sentence-structure/240wz-doc writing-guide-sentence-structure.md Product Intent and AC-6; evidence/README.md step 5
safety_and_authorization: Read-only; no repository edits

disposition_rationale: A one- or two-sentence edit to Product Intent and the README. It must not become a gate.
